question: What is the primary purpose of nursing documentation?

options.A: To provide reading material for incoming medical students
options.B: To serve as a permanent legal record of patient care
options.C: To document disciplinary actions taken against staff
options.D: To fulfill hospital administrative requirements only

explanation: Nursing documentation acts as the definitive legal proof of the nursing assessments, interventions, and evaluations provided to a patient throughout their hospital stay. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is accurate documentation especially critical in high-turnover healthcare environments?

options.A: It reduces the need for doctors to visit the wards daily
options.B: It prevents incoming shifts from forgetting critical patient details
options.C: it lowers the cost of purchasing paper record books
options.D: It eliminates the necessity for verbal shift handovers

explanation: Written records bridge the gap between changing nursing shifts, ensuring that crucial clinical data is never lost despite heavy workloads and busy wards. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which group relies on patient records as a primary tool for interprofessional communication?
explanation: Doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and therapists all read and write in the patient record to coordinate safe, unified daily treatment plans. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h2)

question: How do patient records contribute to public health surveillance?

options.A: By providing de-identified data for tracking disease outbreaks
options.B: By generating monthly salary reports for ministry officials
options.C: By advertising local hospital bed capacities to the public
options.D: By publishing patients' private medical histories in local newspapers

explanation: Aggregated, anonymized data extracted from health records allows epidemiologists to monitor disease trends and plan public health interventions. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h2)

question: Who holds legal ownership of the physical or electronic patient health record?
explanation: While the clinical information inside belongs to the patient, the physical folder, digital database, and paper charts are the property of the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which action represents a direct breach of ethical and legal documentation guidelines?

options.A: Allowing the attending doctor to read the latest laboratory results
options.B: Writing nursing notes using a black ink ballpoint pen
options.C: Filing the completed paper chart in the central records room
options.D: Leaving an open patient chart unattended at the nurses' station

explanation: Leaving records exposed violates patient confidentiality by allowing unauthorized individuals to view private health information. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary issue with writing 'patient had a good night' in a nursing note?

options.A: It takes too much time to write during a busy shift
options.B: It must be written in red ink instead of blue
options.D: It is vague and lacks objective clinical data

explanation: Subjective phrases mean different things to different readers; quality notes require specific, measurable observations about sleep, pain levels, and vitals. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h4)

question: A nurse administers 50mg of tramadol at 14:00. When is the best time to document this administration?

options.B: At the end of the shift around 19:00
options.C: The following morning during the handover meeting

explanation: Documentation must be current and timely; recording care before it happens or waiting until shift change risks omission and inaccuracies. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the defining feature of Charting by Exception?

options.A: Records are kept exclusively on paper folders without digital backups
options.B: Only abnormal findings or deviations from norms are documented
options.C: Every single routine nursing intervention is written in full detail
options.D: Only physicians are permitted to make entries in the chart

explanation: Charting by exception assumes all standard care and normal parameters are met unless a specific exception is explicitly written down. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is a problem-oriented medical record effective for interprofessional collaboration?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever viewing their own clinical files
options.B: All disciplines contribute notes around a centralized list of patient problems
options.C: It completely replaces the need for verbal shift reports
options.D: It separates nurses, doctors, and pharmacists into isolated record sections

explanation: A shared problem list ensures every health professional focuses on and contributes to the same active clinical issues. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h5)

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication framework stand for?
explanation: SBAR provides a standardized structure for clinicians to relay critical patient updates efficiently and accurately. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is a major advantage of using a structured reporting tool during a shift handover?

options.A: It eliminates the need for written nursing care plans
options.B: It ensures handovers always take less than two minutes
options.C: It prevents critical clinical details from being omitted
options.D: It allows nurses to skip reviewing the patient's physical chart

explanation: Standardized frameworks keep the conversation focused on vital health data, reducing the risk that important changes in status get left out. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of filing an institutional incident report?

options.A: To promote quality improvement and prevent future occurrences
options.B: To provide immediate grounds for staff termination
options.C: To serve as part of the patient's permanent clinical chart
options.D: To inform the patient's family of staff disciplinary actions

explanation: Incident reports are quality improvement tools used by facility management to analyze safety gaps and redesign safer clinical systems. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h7)

question: Where should a nurse record the fact that an incident report was completed?

options.A: In the progress notes right after the vital signs
options.B: In bold letters at the very top of the nursing care plan
options.C: On the front cover of the patient's bedside folder
options.D: Nowhere in the patient's clinical medical record

explanation: Incident reports are kept entirely separate from the patient chart; referencing them in clinical notes can compromise legal and administrative reviews. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h7)

question: How should a nurse properly correct a written error in a paper patient chart?

options.A: Tear the page out of the register and start a fresh sheet
options.B: Scratch the incorrect word out completely until it is unreadable
options.C: Draw a single line through the mistake, write 'error', and sign it
options.D: Apply liquid correction fluid over the word and write on top

explanation: A single strikethrough preserves legibility of the original error while clearly showing it was corrected, avoiding any suspicion of document tampering. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why is charting care before it is actually performed considered a serious legal hazard?

options.A: It automatically increases the patient's hospital bill
options.B: It falsifies the medical record and misrepresents clinical timelines
options.C: It prevents the doctor from prescribing new medications
options.D: It causes the hospital computer system to freeze or crash

explanation: Documenting proactive actions before they happen is legally considered falsification of records, as unforeseen emergencies could prevent execution. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h8)
